headline: Fenix Flexin admits to using AI for hit song 'Rubberz,' reversing prior denials
summary: The LA rapper now claims he "never said I didn't use AI," following producer allegations and AI detection of his track 'Rubberz.'
details: LA rapper Fenix Flexin appears to have admitted to using AI for his song "Rubberz," reversing previous denials. This comes after producer Medasin claimed an AI tool called Treblo was used, and the company released an AI detector confirming the song's origin.

Flexin responded to a comment on Instagram, stating, "never said I didn’t use AI, i said it had nun to do w recording process." He added that he was unaware of the app until others commented and that using new technology as a tool is acceptable to stay current.
This statement contradicts his earlier public stance. Last month, during an interview on Hot 97’s Mornings With Mero, Flexin explicitly stated, "no AI on it" when asked directly about AI use.

Previously, Fenix and his team had shared what they presented as recording session files, insisted the song was made by two humans using Pro Tools, auto-tune, and reverb, and claimed he was singing live in clips where he appeared to be lip-syncing.
caption:
Fenix Flexin reverses course, now admitting to using AI for his hit song 'Rubberz' after previously denying it.

LA rapper Fenix Flexin appears to have admitted to using AI for his song "Rubberz," reversing previous denials. This comes after producer Medasin claimed an AI tool called Treblo was used, and the company released an AI detector confirming the song's origin.

Flexin responded to a comment on Instagram, stating, "never said I didn’t use AI, i said it had nun to do w recording process." He added that he was unaware of the app until others commented and that using new technology as a tool is acceptable to stay current.

This statement contradicts his earlier public stance. Last month, during an interview on Hot 97’s Mornings With Mero, Flexin explicitly stated, "no AI on it" when asked directly about AI use.

Previously, Fenix and his team had shared what they presented as recording session files, insisted the song was made by two humans using Pro Tools, auto-tune, and reverb, and claimed he was singing live in clips where he appeared to be lip-syncing.
